name: Operation Overlord Planning and Preparation - Historical: Meticulous Preparation
description: Eisenhower appointed Supreme Commander with Montgomery commanding 21st Army Group. Deception operations (Fortitude North/South) deceive Germans about Pas-de-Calais. Massive buildup in southern England with 2 million troops.
historical_context: After years of 'Second Front Now' pressure from Stalin and delayed by Mediterranean commitments, the Allies committed to invading Normandy. Britain provided bases, intelligence, naval supremacy, and significant ground forces despite manpower constraints.

name: Operation Overlord Planning and Preparation - Alternative: Rushed Preparation
description: Soviet pressure and American impatience force earlier invasion date with less preparation. Deception operations less extensive. Some equipment shortfalls.
historical_context: After years of 'Second Front Now' pressure from Stalin and delayed by Mediterranean commitments, the Allies committed to invading Normandy. Britain provided bases, intelligence, naval supremacy, and significant ground forces despite manpower constraints.

name: Operation Overlord Planning and Preparation - Radical: Mediterranean Priority
description: Churchill successfully argues for continued Mediterranean focus, postponing Overlord to 1945. Adriatic landings toward Austria prioritized.
historical_context: After years of 'Second Front Now' pressure from Stalin and delayed by Mediterranean commitments, the Allies committed to invading Normandy. Britain provided bases, intelligence, naval supremacy, and significant ground forces despite manpower constraints.

name: D-Day: Operation Overlord - Historical: Successful Lodgement
description: Despite fierce resistance and failure to achieve all D-Day objectives (particularly Caen), Allied forces establish solid beachheads. Gold, Juno, and Sword beaches secured with British 50th Division, Canadian 3rd Division, and British 3rd Division.
historical_context: After four years of German occupation and three years of planning, the Western Allies returned to the continent. British and Canadian forces landed on three beaches with objectives to capture Caen and link up with American forces.

name: D-Day: Operation Overlord - Alternative: Costly Stalemate
description: German defenses prove more formidable than expected. Rommel's beach obstacles and strong counterattacks contain Allied beachheads. Heavy casualties on all beaches.
historical_context: After four years of German occupation and three years of planning, the Western Allies returned to the continent. British and Canadian forces landed on three beaches with objectives to capture Caen and link up with American forces.

name: D-Day: Operation Overlord - Radical: Catastrophic Failure
description: German intelligence penetrates Fortitude deception. Panzer reserves positioned near Normandy. Allied landings met with overwhelming force. Potential Dunkirk-scale evacuation required.
historical_context: After four years of German occupation and three years of planning, the Western Allies returned to the continent. British and Canadian forces landed on three beaches with objectives to capture Caen and link up with American forces.

name: Battle for Caen - Historical: Attritional Victory
description: After multiple failed attempts (Perch, Epsom, Charnwood, Goodwood), Caen finally falls in late July. British armor suffers heavy losses but pins German Panzers, enabling American Operation Cobra breakout.
historical_context: Caen was meant to fall on D-Day. Instead, it became the focus of British/Canadian efforts through June and July, drawing German armor away from American breakout sector - exactly as Montgomery (controversially) claimed was his plan.

name: Battle for Caen - Alternative: Swift Capture
description: Aggressive armored thrust in mid-June breaks through German defenses. Caen falls with moderate casualties. Montgomery vindicated.
historical_context: Caen was meant to fall on D-Day. Instead, it became the focus of British/Canadian efforts through June and July, drawing German armor away from American breakout sector - exactly as Montgomery (controversially) claimed was his plan.

name: Battle for Caen - Radical: Caen Stalemate
description: Repeated British attacks fail catastrophically. Caen becomes WWI-style stalemate. American breakout also stalls without German forces pinned. Normandy campaign bogs down into autumn.
historical_context: Caen was meant to fall on D-Day. Instead, it became the focus of British/Canadian efforts through June and July, drawing German armor away from American breakout sector - exactly as Montgomery (controversially) claimed was his plan.

name: V-1 Flying Bomb Campaign - Historical: Effective Countermeasures
description: British defenses improve dramatically. Fighter aircraft (especially Tempests and Spitfire XIVs), anti-aircraft guns with proximity fuses, and barrage balloons shoot down ~80% of V-1s by August. Operation Crossbow bombs launch sites.
historical_context: Hitler's 'Vengeance Weapons' came too late to affect war's outcome but terrorized civilians. V-1 attacks killed ~6,000 Britons. Defense required massive resource allocation to anti-aircraft guns, fighters, and Operation Crossbow targeting launch sites.

name: V-1 Flying Bomb Campaign - Alternative: Devastating Campaign
description: British defenses less effective. V-1 accuracy improved. ~50% reach targets. Civilian casualties triple. Morale significantly impacted.
historical_context: Hitler's 'Vengeance Weapons' came too late to affect war's outcome but terrorized civilians. V-1 attacks killed ~6,000 Britons. Defense required massive resource allocation to anti-aircraft guns, fighters, and Operation Crossbow targeting launch sites.

name: V-1 Flying Bomb Campaign - Radical: V-Weapon Launch Prevented
description: Operation Crossbow intelligence and bombing campaign destroys V-weapon program before launch. Peenemünde scientists captured or killed. Hitler's vengeance weapons never deployed.
historical_context: Hitler's 'Vengeance Weapons' came too late to affect war's outcome but terrorized civilians. V-1 attacks killed ~6,000 Britons. Defense required massive resource allocation to anti-aircraft guns, fighters, and Operation Crossbow targeting launch sites.

name: Operation Market Garden - Historical: Bridge Too Far
description: American 101st and 82nd Airborne secure Eindhoven and Nijmegen bridges. British 1st Airborne at Arnhem runs into unexpected SS Panzer divisions. XXX Corps advance delayed on narrow road. Arnhem bridge held heroically but relieving force arrives too late. Operation fails.
historical_context: After breakout from Normandy and liberation of France/Belgium, Montgomery proposed daring thrust into Netherlands to outflank Siegfried Line, cross Rhine, and potentially end war in 1944. Required three airborne divisions to seize bridges for XXX Corps armored advance.

name: Operation Market Garden - Alternative: Complete Success
description: All bridges captured and held. XXX Corps reaches Arnhem within 48 hours. Rhine crossed. Ruhr outflanked. German defenses collapse. War potentially ends in 1944.
historical_context: After breakout from Normandy and liberation of France/Belgium, Montgomery proposed daring thrust into Netherlands to outflank Siegfried Line, cross Rhine, and potentially end war in 1944. Required three airborne divisions to seize bridges for XXX Corps armored advance.

name: Operation Market Garden - Radical: Catastrophic Failure
description: German intelligence aware of plan. Massive trap set. All three airborne divisions destroyed. XXX Corps ambushed. Worst Allied defeat in Western Europe.
historical_context: After breakout from Normandy and liberation of France/Belgium, Montgomery proposed daring thrust into Netherlands to outflank Siegfried Line, cross Rhine, and potentially end war in 1944. Required three airborne divisions to seize bridges for XXX Corps armored advance.

name: Liberation of France and Belgium - Historical: Rapid Liberation
description: British Second Army and Canadian First Army race through France and Belgium. Le Havre, Dieppe, Boulogne, Calais liberated. Brussels freed September 3rd. Antwerp captured September 4th but Scheldt Estuary remains German, hampering port use.
historical_context: After grinding Normandy battles, German defensive line collapsed in August. Allied armies achieved operational mobility dreamed of since D-Day. British and Canadian forces liberated Northern France and Belgium while Americans drove toward Germany.

name: Liberation of France and Belgium - Alternative: Methodical Advance
description: Montgomery insists on slower, more cautious advance ensuring supply lines secure. Liberation delayed but more organized. Scheldt cleared earlier, opening Antwerp by October.
historical_context: After grinding Normandy battles, German defensive line collapsed in August. Allied armies achieved operational mobility dreamed of since D-Day. British and Canadian forces liberated Northern France and Belgium while Americans drove toward Germany.

name: Liberation of France and Belgium - Radical: Stalled Offensive
description: German defenses stabilize after Normandy. Liberation of France and Belgium becomes protracted affair. Paris not liberated until late 1944. Belgium remains contested into 1945.
historical_context: After grinding Normandy battles, German defensive line collapsed in August. Allied armies achieved operational mobility dreamed of since D-Day. British and Canadian forces liberated Northern France and Belgium while Americans drove toward Germany.

name: Strategic Bomber Offensive Intensifies - Historical: Maximum Effort
description: Bomber Command flies 297,663 sorties in 1944, dropping 525,000 tons of bombs. Attacks on French transportation pre-D-Day, oil facilities, German cities. Dresden bombing February 1945 kills tens of thousands. German war production peaks despite bombing but collapses late 1944.
historical_context: 1944 saw peak of Allied strategic bombing. RAF bombed at night, USAAF by day. Attacks on transportation, oil, and cities. Questions about civilian casualties and actual impact on German war production. Churchill began distancing himself from 'area bombing' policy.

name: Strategic Bomber Offensive Intensifies - Alternative: Precision Focus
description: British shift to precision bombing of military/industrial targets. Reduced civilian casualties. Greater emphasis on oil and transportation. Area bombing curtailed earlier.
historical_context: 1944 saw peak of Allied strategic bombing. RAF bombed at night, USAAF by day. Attacks on transportation, oil, and cities. Questions about civilian casualties and actual impact on German war production. Churchill began distancing himself from 'area bombing' policy.

name: Strategic Bomber Offensive Intensifies - Radical: Bomber Offensive Curtailed
description: Growing losses and moral concerns lead to early curtailment of strategic bombing. Resources redirected to tactical air support and anti-submarine warfare.
historical_context: 1944 saw peak of Allied strategic bombing. RAF bombed at night, USAAF by day. Attacks on transportation, oil, and cities. Questions about civilian casualties and actual impact on German war production. Churchill began distancing himself from 'area bombing' policy.

name: Burma Campaign: Imphal and Kohima - Historical: Slim's Masterpiece
description: Japanese offensive initially successful, besieging Imphal and Kohima. British-Indian forces supplied by air. Slim's tactical brilliance and Japanese logistical failure lead to crushing Allied victory. Japanese suffer ~53,000 casualties including 30,000 dead.
historical_context: Churchill called Burma the 'Forgotten War' - overshadowed by European theater. Yet here British and Indian forces fought Japan's largest land defeat of the war. William Slim's 14th Army ('The Forgotten Army') proved superior in jungle warfare.

name: Burma Campaign: Imphal and Kohima - Alternative: Costly Stalemate
description: Japanese offensive makes deeper penetration. Imphal siege prolonged. British-Indian counterattacks less effective. Both sides suffer heavy casualties. Burma campaign stalemated into 1945.
historical_context: Churchill called Burma the 'Forgotten War' - overshadowed by European theater. Yet here British and Indian forces fought Japan's largest land defeat of the war. William Slim's 14th Army ('The Forgotten Army') proved superior in jungle warfare.

name: Burma Campaign: Imphal and Kohima - Radical: Japanese Breakthrough
description: Japanese Operation U-Go succeeds. Imphal and Kohima fall. Japanese invade Assam. India's security threatened. Churchill forced to divert resources from Europe. War in Asia prolonged significantly.
historical_context: Churchill called Burma the 'Forgotten War' - overshadowed by European theater. Yet here British and Indian forces fought Japan's largest land defeat of the war. William Slim's 14th Army ('The Forgotten Army') proved superior in jungle warfare.

name: Yalta Conference - Historical: Difficult Compromises
description: Churchill fights for Poland and Eastern Europe but ultimately accepts Soviet sphere of influence. Germany to be divided into occupation zones. Free elections promised in liberated territories (promise soon broken). UN charter agreed. Soviet entry into Pacific War confirmed.
historical_context: With victory in sight, the Grand Alliance began planning the peace. Churchill arrived at Yalta weakened - Britain exhausted by war, American power ascendant, Soviet armies occupying Eastern Europe. The conference shaped the post-war world and sowed seeds of Cold War.

name: Yalta Conference - Alternative: Churchill's Hard Line
description: Churchill takes harder stance on Eastern Europe, backed by threatened British withdrawal from alliance. Roosevelt supports British position. Stalin makes greater concessions on Poland and Balkans. More genuine free elections guaranteed.
historical_context: With victory in sight, the Grand Alliance began planning the peace. Churchill arrived at Yalta weakened - Britain exhausted by war, American power ascendant, Soviet armies occupying Eastern Europe. The conference shaped the post-war world and sowed seeds of Cold War.

name: Yalta Conference - Radical: Alliance Breakdown
description: Fundamental disagreements over Eastern Europe cannot be bridged. Yalta Conference fails. Separate peace negotiations begin. Grand Alliance fractures before German surrender. Race for Berlin becomes hostile competition.
historical_context: With victory in sight, the Grand Alliance began planning the peace. Churchill arrived at Yalta weakened - Britain exhausted by war, American power ascendant, Soviet armies occupying Eastern Europe. The conference shaped the post-war world and sowed seeds of Cold War.

name: Crossing the Rhine - Historical: Overwhelming Success
description: After massive artillery bombardment and air support, British and Canadian forces cross Rhine with relatively light casualties. Airborne divisions seize key objectives. Bridgeheads rapidly expanded. German resistance collapsing.
historical_context: Rhine crossing represented entry into Germany proper. Montgomery planned meticulously, massing overwhelming force. Airborne operation (Varsity) largest single-day airborne assault. Contrast with American opportunistic Remagen crossing days earlier.

name: Crossing the Rhine - Alternative: Costly Assault
description: German resistance stiffer than expected. Airborne losses heavy. Rhine crossing succeeds but at significant cost. Advance into Germany slowed. Americans achieve greater success, further overshadowing British effort.
historical_context: Rhine crossing represented entry into Germany proper. Montgomery planned meticulously, massing overwhelming force. Airborne operation (Varsity) largest single-day airborne assault. Contrast with American opportunistic Remagen crossing days earlier.

name: Crossing the Rhine - Radical: Race for Berlin Authorized
description: Churchill convinces Eisenhower to authorize Montgomery's thrust to Berlin. British forces advance rapidly northeast instead of clearing northern Germany. British reach Berlin before or simultaneously with Soviets.
historical_context: Rhine crossing represented entry into Germany proper. Montgomery planned meticulously, massing overwhelming force. Airborne operation (Varsity) largest single-day airborne assault. Contrast with American opportunistic Remagen crossing days earlier.

name: Liberation of Concentration Camps - Historical: Horror Revealed
description: British 11th Armoured Division liberates Belsen April 15th. Shocked soldiers discover thousands of corpses, emaciated survivors, typhus epidemic. Medical teams save many but ~14,000 die after liberation. Evidence meticulously documented. World learns of Holocaust's reality through newsreels and photographs.
historical_context: While Allied leaders knew of Nazi persecution, the concentration camps' liberation revealed genocide's full scale. British forces at Belsen found scenes beyond comprehension. Medical teams struggled to save survivors. Evidence documented for war crimes trials.

name: Liberation of Concentration Camps - Alternative: Earlier Liberation
description: If British advance faster in 1944, camps liberated months earlier. Thousands more survivors saved. Greater evidence preserved. More perpetrators captured. Earlier awareness of Holocaust scale.
historical_context: While Allied leaders knew of Nazi persecution, the concentration camps' liberation revealed genocide's full scale. British forces at Belsen found scenes beyond comprehension. Medical teams struggled to save survivors. Evidence documented for war crimes trials.

name: German Surrender - Historical: Unconditional Surrender
description: Germany surrenders unconditionally. VE-Day celebrations across Britain May 8th. Churchill addresses crowds: 'This is your victory.' Rationing continues. Reality sets in - Japan remains, empire challenged, Soviet threat looming, economy shattered. But Hitler defeated.
historical_context: Hitler's suicide April 30th led to German capitulation. Surrender signed at Reims (May 7) and Berlin (May 8-9). Britain exhausted but victorious. Price: 450,000 dead, empire weakened, massive debt. But Nazi tyranny destroyed.

name: German Surrender - Alternative: Conditional Surrender
description: German military forces capitulate but conditional terms negotiated. Wehrmacht remains partially intact. Different occupation arrangement. War crimes trials complicated. Cold War begins differently.
historical_context: Hitler's suicide April 30th led to German capitulation. Surrender signed at Reims (May 7) and Berlin (May 8-9). Britain exhausted but victorious. Price: 450,000 dead, empire weakened, massive debt. But Nazi tyranny destroyed.

name: German Surrender - Radical: Protracted Endgame
description: German resistance continues in Alpine Redoubt or via guerrilla warfare. Surrender delayed to late 1945 or 1946. Higher casualties. British exhaustion even more severe. Different atomic bomb use scenario.
historical_context: Hitler's suicide April 30th led to German capitulation. Surrender signed at Reims (May 7) and Berlin (May 8-9). Britain exhausted but victorious. Price: 450,000 dead, empire weakened, massive debt. But Nazi tyranny destroyed.

name: Churchill's Election Defeat - Historical: Labour Landslide
description: Labour wins 393 seats vs Conservatives' 213. Massive 12% swing. Churchill shocked. Attlee to Potsdam mid-conference to replace Churchill. Labour begins implementing socialist program: NHS, nationalization, welfare state. Churchill leads opposition. Imperial preference vs American loan debate.
historical_context: While Churchill led nation through war, British voters wanted post-war social change. Labour promised welfare state, NHS, nationalization. Churchill's 'Gestapo' speech backfired. Servicemen voted overwhelmingly Labour. Remarkable democratic moment - victorious war leader peacefully replaced.

name: Churchill's Election Defeat - Alternative: Churchill Victory
description: Churchill's prestige carries Conservatives to victory. Labour gains but no majority. Churchill continues as PM, focuses on foreign policy and empire. Different approach to decolonization, welfare state, relationship with USA and USSR.
historical_context: While Churchill led nation through war, British voters wanted post-war social change. Labour promised welfare state, NHS, nationalization. Churchill's 'Gestapo' speech backfired. Servicemen voted overwhelmingly Labour. Remarkable democratic moment - victorious war leader peacefully replaced.

name: Churchill's Election Defeat - Radical: National Government Continued
description: Coalition government continues into peacetime. Churchill remains PM with Labour participation. Consensus politics on welfare state and foreign policy. Different political culture emerges.
historical_context: While Churchill led nation through war, British voters wanted post-war social change. Labour promised welfare state, NHS, nationalization. Churchill's 'Gestapo' speech backfired. Servicemen voted overwhelmingly Labour. Remarkable democratic moment - victorious war leader peacefully replaced.

name: Potsdam Conference - Historical: Divided Europe Confirmed
description: Germany divided into occupation zones. Poland's western border at Oder-Neisse line. German reparations agreed (Soviets strip Eastern zone). Free elections promise for Eastern Europe (not honored). Atomic bomb mentioned to Stalin. Potsdam Declaration warns Japan. Cold War division solidifying.
historical_context: Last meeting of Grand Alliance. Stalin dominated, controlling Eastern Europe. Truman replaced Roosevelt, tougher on Soviets. Attlee replaced Churchill mid-conference - remarkable democratic moment. Decisions shaped divided Europe. Atomic bomb's shadow over proceedings.

name: Potsdam Conference - Alternative: Tougher Western Stance
description: If Churchill remained PM or if Attlee/Truman take harder line. Atomic monopoly leveraged. Genuine free elections in Eastern Europe demanded and partially achieved. Different German settlement. Soviet sphere smaller.
historical_context: Last meeting of Grand Alliance. Stalin dominated, controlling Eastern Europe. Truman replaced Roosevelt, tougher on Soviets. Attlee replaced Churchill mid-conference - remarkable democratic moment. Decisions shaped divided Europe. Atomic bomb's shadow over proceedings.

name: Potsdam Conference - Radical: Cooperation Maintained
description: Genuine attempt at post-war cooperation with USSR. Atomic bomb shared via international authority. Germany reunified under joint supervision. Eastern European settlement negotiated. Cold War avoided or delayed. Naïve or visionary?
historical_context: Last meeting of Grand Alliance. Stalin dominated, controlling Eastern Europe. Truman replaced Roosevelt, tougher on Soviets. Attlee replaced Churchill mid-conference - remarkable democratic moment. Decisions shaped divided Europe. Atomic bomb's shadow over proceedings.

name: Japan's Surrender and War's End - Historical: Atomic Ending
description: Hiroshima (Aug 6) and Nagasaki (Aug 9) atomic bombings plus Soviet invasion of Manchuria force Japanese surrender. British minor role in final phase but significant in Burma. Emperor announces surrender Aug 15. VJ-Day Aug 15 (UK) and Sept 2 (formal). Britain demobilizes, faces peace.
historical_context: Britain played supporting role in Pacific War but significant forces engaged in Burma and with Pacific Fleet. Japanese surrender ended WWII globally. Britain could finally demobilize fully and focus on reconstruction. But empire's future uncertain and Cold War emerging.

name: Japan's Surrender and War's End - Alternative: Invasion Scenario
description: No atomic bombs (program fails or ethical rejection). Conventional invasion of Japan required. British forces participate in Operation Downfall. War extends into 1946. Hundreds of thousands more casualties. Soviet role in Japan larger. Different post-war Pacific settlement.
historical_context: Britain played supporting role in Pacific War but significant forces engaged in Burma and with Pacific Fleet. Japanese surrender ended WWII globally. Britain could finally demobilize fully and focus on reconstruction. But empire's future uncertain and Cold War emerging.

name: Japan's Surrender and War's End - Radical: Conditional Surrender
description: Japan negotiates conditional surrender preserving emperor and some territorial claims. War ends without atomic bombs or invasion. Different occupation arrangement. Imperial system maintained. Soviet gains limited. Different post-war Asia.
historical_context: Britain played supporting role in Pacific War but significant forces engaged in Burma and with Pacific Fleet. Japanese surrender ended WWII globally. Britain could finally demobilize fully and focus on reconstruction. But empire's future uncertain and Cold War emerging.

name: Post-War Reckoning and New World Order - Historical: Managed Decline and Social Revolution
description: Attlee government manages extraordinary transition. American loan negotiated (harsh terms). India independence 1947. Palestine abandoned 1948. NHS created 1948. Nationalization of industries. Marshall Plan aid. NATO membership 1949. Empire dissolves but Commonwealth emerges. Nuclear weapons developed. 'Special relationship' with USA. Relative decline managed while creating welfare state.
historical_context: Victory's price: Britain ended war victorious but impoverished. National debt 250% GDP. Empire untenable. Replaced as world's greatest power by USA and challenged by USSR. Yet created NHS, welfare state, maintained democracy, contributed to UN, NATO. Remarkable transition from total war to peaceful social revolution.

name: Post-War Reckoning and New World Order - Alternative: Imperial Persistence
description: If Churchill won 1945 election or if different decisions made - attempt to maintain empire longer. More resources to colonial wars. Slower welfare state development. Different relationship with USA. India independence delayed/contested. Palestine held longer. Suez not abandoned. More confrontational Cold War stance. Unsustainable?
historical_context: Victory's price: Britain ended war victorious but impoverished. National debt 250% GDP. Empire untenable. Replaced as world's greatest power by USA and challenged by USSR. Yet created NHS, welfare state, maintained democracy, contributed to UN, NATO. Remarkable transition from total war to peaceful social revolution.

name: Post-War Reckoning and New World Order - Radical: European Leadership
description: Britain embraces European integration immediately post-war. Joins/leads European Coal-Steel Community 1951, European Economic Community 1957. European focus vs Atlantic/Commonwealth. Different British identity. Leadership of European unity. Potential European superpower rather than American junior partner.
historical_context: Victory's price: Britain ended war victorious but impoverished. National debt 250% GDP. Empire untenable. Replaced as world's greatest power by USA and challenged by USSR. name: Operation Barbarossa Begins - Historical: Border Catastrophe
description: German surprise attack achieves complete tactical and operational surprise. Soviet Western Front, Northwestern Front, Southwestern Front shattered in first hours. Entire air force destroyed on ground. Communications collapse. Stalin suffers breakdown for several days. Red Army loses 2.5 million men in first six weeks.
historical_context: Despite numerous intelligence warnings (Richard Sorge, Lucy Spy Ring, British warnings), Stalin refused to believe Hitler would attack. Soviet forces on border were in peacetime deployment. Purges of 1937-38 had killed most experienced commanders. Result: worst military disaster in history.

name: Operation Barbarossa Begins - Alternative: Prepared Defense
description: Stalin heeds warnings. Red Army on alert. Border forces in defensive positions. Luftwaffe encounters resistance. Initial German advance slowed. Casualties still heavy but armies intact. Different war from day one.
historical_context: Despite numerous intelligence warnings (Richard Sorge, Lucy Spy Ring, British warnings), Stalin refused to believe Hitler would attack. Soviet forces on border were in peacetime deployment. Purges of 1937-38 had killed most experienced commanders. Result: worst military disaster in history.

name: Operation Barbarossa Begins - Radical: Preemptive Strike
description: Stalin orders preemptive attack on German concentrations. Red Army strikes first but from poor positions with inferior doctrine. Initial chaos but different strategic situation. Propaganda victory for Hitler. Different war entirely.
historical_context: Despite numerous intelligence warnings (Richard Sorge, Lucy Spy Ring, British warnings), Stalin refused to believe Hitler would attack. Soviet forces on border were in peacetime deployment. Purges of 1937-38 had killed most experienced commanders. Result: worst military disaster in history.

name: Battle of Smolensk - Historical: Costly Delay
description: Fierce Soviet resistance around Smolensk. Multiple encirclements but surrounded troops fight on for weeks. German advance slowed from 20 miles/day to 5 miles/day. Hitler diverts Guderian south to Ukraine. Moscow offensive delayed to October - crucial respite.
historical_context: Smolensk was gateway to Moscow. Soviet resistance here was far stiffer than Germans expected. First indication that blitzkrieg might not work in Russia. Two months bought time for Moscow defenses and Siberian reinforcements. Hitler faces first major decision: Moscow or Ukraine?

name: Battle of Smolensk - Alternative: Rapid Collapse
description: Smolensk falls quickly without effective resistance. Germans maintain momentum. Hitler doesn't divert to Ukraine. Drive on Moscow begins in August with full force. Moscow potentially falls before winter.
historical_context: Smolensk was gateway to Moscow. Soviet resistance here was far stiffer than Germans expected. First indication that blitzkrieg might not work in Russia. Two months bought time for Moscow defenses and Siberian reinforcements. Hitler faces first major decision: Moscow or Ukraine?

name: Battle of Smolensk - Radical: Major Counteroffensive Success
description: Soviet counterattacks at Smolensk achieve major success. German salients cut off. First major Red Army victory. German casualties enormous. Barbarossa potentially derailed entirely. Over-optimism danger.
historical_context: Smolensk was gateway to Moscow. Soviet resistance here was far stiffer than Germans expected. First indication that blitzkrieg might not work in Russia. Two months bought time for Moscow defenses and Siberian reinforcements. Hitler faces first major decision: Moscow or Ukraine?

name: Kiev Encirclement Disaster - Historical: 'Hold at All Costs' Catastrophe
description: Stalin orders 'not one step back' at Kiev despite encirclement threat. Commanders who suggest retreat (including Zhukov) dismissed. German pincers close. 665,000 Soviets trapped in largest encirclement ever. All heavy equipment lost. But Moscow gets more time.
historical_context: Stalin's stubbornness caused worst Soviet defeat of war. Zhukov advocated retreat - Stalin fired him. Guderian's panzers diverted from Moscow drive to complete encirclement. Military catastrophe but strategic consequence unclear - Moscow drive delayed further.

name: Kiev Encirclement Disaster - Alternative: Authorized Retreat
description: Stalin listens to Zhukov. Kiev abandoned. Southwestern Front retreats in good order. 500,000+ troops saved to fight another day. Ukraine falls faster but army intact. Germans advance on Moscow earlier.
historical_context: Stalin's stubbornness caused worst Soviet defeat of war. Zhukov advocated retreat - Stalin fired him. Guderian's panzers diverted from Moscow drive to complete encirclement. Military catastrophe but strategic consequence unclear - Moscow drive delayed further.

name: Kiev Encirclement Disaster - Radical: Successful Kiev Defense
description: Kiev held through brilliant defense and counterattacks. German encirclement attempt fails. Southwestern Front intact. Ukraine battle becomes protracted. Moscow threatened less but resources consumed.
historical_context: Stalin's stubbornness caused worst Soviet defeat of war. Zhukov advocated retreat - Stalin fired him. Guderian's panzers diverted from Moscow drive to complete encirclement. Military catastrophe but strategic consequence unclear - Moscow drive delayed further.

name: Siege of Leningrad Begins - Historical: The 900-Day Siege
description: City encircled September 8. All land routes cut. Only supply via Lake Ladoga. Rations reduced to 125g bread/day. First winter catastrophic: hundreds of thousands starve. But Leningrad never surrenders. 'Road of Life' maintains minimal supply. Shostakovich's 7th Symphony performed during siege. Symbol of resistance.
historical_context: Hitler ordered Leningrad wiped from face of earth. City of Lenin, birthplace of Revolution. Germans settled for siege rather than direct assault. Resulted in humanitarian catastrophe - ~1 million died, mostly from starvation. But city never surrendered, inspiring symbol.

name: Siege of Leningrad Begins - Alternative: Successful Evacuation
description: More time before encirclement allows mass civilian evacuation. Military priority given to breaking siege early. City's population reduced to defenders and essential workers. Casualties much lower but symbolic value less.
historical_context: Hitler ordered Leningrad wiped from face of earth. City of Lenin, birthplace of Revolution. Germans settled for siege rather than direct assault. Resulted in humanitarian catastrophe - ~1 million died, mostly from starvation. But city never surrendered, inspiring symbol.

name: Siege of Leningrad Begins - Radical: City Falls
description: German direct assault succeeds or siege forces surrender. Leningrad falls. Massive propaganda defeat. Soviet morale crisis. Hitler razes city as planned. But German forces freed for Moscow offensive.
historical_context: Hitler ordered Leningrad wiped from face of earth. City of Lenin, birthplace of Revolution. Germans settled for siege rather than direct assault. Resulted in humanitarian catastrophe - ~1 million died, mostly from starvation. But city never surrendered, inspiring symbol.

name: Battle of Moscow Begins - Historical: Moscow Holds
description: Operation Typhoon begins October 2. Initial success - Vyazma encirclement bags 600,000. Germans reach Moscow suburbs by December. But Siberian divisions arrive. Winter hits. German equipment freezes. Stalin stays in city. Zhukov's defense holds. Germans exhaust themselves at gates of Moscow.
historical_context: Hitler's final gamble for 1941 victory. Delayed by Kiev and Smolensk. October mud slowed advance. November cold froze Germans. December brought Siberian divisions and counteroffensive. Closest Germans came to winning on Eastern Front. Moscow's survival ensured prolonged war.

name: Battle of Moscow Begins - Alternative: Moscow Falls
description: Earlier German offensive or later winter or Siberian divisions delayed. Moscow falls in December 1941. Stalin captured or flees. Soviet state potentially collapses or continues from Urals. Different war entirely. But German victory far from certain - vast space remains.
historical_context: Hitler's final gamble for 1941 victory. Delayed by Kiev and Smolensk. October mud slowed advance. November cold froze Germans. December brought Siberian divisions and counteroffensive. Closest Germans came to winning on Eastern Front. Moscow's survival ensured prolonged war.

name: Battle of Moscow Begins - Radical: Decisive Counteroffensive Victory
description: Moscow defense combined with massive early counteroffensive. German Army Group Center encircled and destroyed. Wehrmacht's eastern army eliminated. War potentially won in 1941-42. Over-optimistic but shows possibilities.
historical_context: Hitler's final gamble for 1941 victory. Delayed by Kiev and Smolensk. October mud slowed advance. November cold froze Germans. December brought Siberian divisions and counteroffensive. Closest Germans came to winning on Eastern Front. Moscow's survival ensured prolonged war.

name: Winter Counteroffensive - Historical: Moscow Relieved, Strategic Overreach
description: December 5 counteroffensive succeeds brilliantly around Moscow. Germans driven back 100-250km. Rostov and Tikhvin also recaptured. But Stalin orders general offensive all along front - beyond Red Army capabilities. Leads to 1942 disasters. Moscow saved but war continues.
historical_context: First major Soviet victory. Shattered myth of German invincibility. Showed Red Army could not just defend but attack. But Stalin's optimism led to overambitious 1942 offensives that failed. Winter counteroffensive saved Moscow but didn't end war as Stalin hoped.

name: Winter Counteroffensive - Alternative: Limited Success and Consolidation
description: Zhukov's advice heeded. Counteroffensive limited to Moscow relief. No general offensive. Strength husbanded for 1942. More defensive operations. Avoids 1942 Kharkov disaster. Different strategic path.
historical_context: First major Soviet victory. Shattered myth of German invincibility. Showed Red Army could not just defend but attack. But Stalin's optimism led to overambitious 1942 offensives that failed. Winter counteroffensive saved Moscow but didn't end war as Stalin hoped.

name: Winter Counteroffensive - Radical: Decisive Winter Victory
description: Perfect winter counteroffensive destroys German Army Group Center entirely. Wehrmacht's eastern army eliminated. War potentially won by spring 1942. Requires everything to go right for Soviets, wrong for Germans.
historical_context: First major Soviet victory. Shattered myth of German invincibility. Showed Red Army could not just defend but attack. But Stalin's optimism led to overambitious 1942 offensives that failed. Winter counteroffensive saved Moscow but didn't end war as Stalin hoped.

name: Rzhev Meat Grinder - Historical: Catastrophic Attrition
description: Repeated frontal assaults on fortified German positions. Operation Mars (November 1942) particularly disastrous - Zhukov's most ambitious offensive fails catastrophically with 350,000 casualties. Stalin and Zhukov suppress information. Salient not eliminated until March 1943 when Germans voluntarily withdraw for strategic reasons.
historical_context: Rzhev salient threatened Moscow. Stalin ordered its elimination repeatedly. Red Army launched multiple offensives: Rzhev-Vyazma (Jan-April), First Rzhev-Sychyovka (July-Aug), Second Rzhev-Sychyovka/Operation Mars (Nov-Dec). All failed with horrific casualties. German Model's defensive mastery. Soviet public didn't learn of disaster until post-Soviet era.

name: Rzhev Meat Grinder - Alternative: Early Withdrawal
description: After initial failures, Stalin accepts Rzhev can't be taken by frontal assault. Resources redirected to Stalingrad and other sectors. Hundreds of thousands of lives saved. Different strategic focus.
historical_context: Rzhev salient threatened Moscow. Stalin ordered its elimination repeatedly. Red Army launched multiple offensives: Rzhev-Vyazma (Jan-April), First Rzhev-Sychyovka (July-Aug), Second Rzhev-Sychyovka/Operation Mars (Nov-Dec). All failed with horrific casualties. German Model's defensive mastery. Soviet public didn't learn of disaster until post-Soviet era.

name: Rzhev Meat Grinder - Radical: Operation Mars Succeeds
description: Zhukov's November offensive achieves breakthrough. Rzhev salient eliminated. German 9th Army encircled. Major victory shifts 1942 narrative. But requires everything to go right.
historical_context: Rzhev salient threatened Moscow. Stalin ordered its elimination repeatedly. Red Army launched multiple offensives: Rzhev-Vyazma (Jan-April), First Rzhev-Sychyovka (July-Aug), Second Rzhev-Sychyovka/Operation Mars (Nov-Dec). All failed with horrific casualties. German Model's defensive mastery. Soviet public didn't learn of disaster until post-Soviet era.

name: Second Battle of Kharkov - Historical: Encirclement Disaster
description: Soviet offensive initially succeeds but German Fridericus counterattack cuts off three armies in Barvenkovo salient. 270,000 casualties, 1,200 tanks lost. Southern front collapses. Germans gain freedom of action for Case Blue summer offensive. Stalin's overconfidence catastrophically punished.
historical_context: Stalin's overconfidence from winter victories led to poorly planned spring offensive. Timoshenko warned of danger but Stalin insisted. Germans under Kleist and Paulus counterattacked brilliantly. Barvenkovo salient became death trap. Opened southern flank for German Case Blue summer offensive toward Caucasus and Stalingrad.

name: Second Battle of Kharkov - Alternative: Offensive Cancelled or Limited
description: Stalin heeds warnings. Kharkov offensive called off or limited to probing attacks. Forces preserved for defense. Case Blue faces prepared Soviet defenses. Stalingrad crisis possibly avoided or mitigated.
historical_context: Stalin's overconfidence from winter victories led to poorly planned spring offensive. Timoshenko warned of danger but Stalin insisted. Germans under Kleist and Paulus counterattacked brilliantly. Barvenkovo salient became death trap. Opened southern flank for German Case Blue summer offensive toward Caucasus and Stalingrad.

name: Second Battle of Kharkov - Radical: Soviet Offensive Succeeds
description: Kharkov offensive achieves objectives. German counterattack fails or doesn't materialize. Major Soviet victory. Case Blue potentially impossible. Different 1942 - Soviets on offensive instead of defensive.
historical_context: Stalin's overconfidence from winter victories led to poorly planned spring offensive. Timoshenko warned of danger but Stalin insisted. Germans under Kleist and Paulus counterattacked brilliantly. Barvenkovo salient became death trap. Opened southern flank for German Case Blue summer offensive toward Caucasus and Stalingrad.

name: Case Blue: German Summer Offensive - Historical: Dual Objectives and Overextension
description: Case Blue begins June 28. Germans race across steppes. Rostov falls July 23. Hitler then divides: Group A (Kleist) to Caucasus, Group B (Paulus) to Stalingrad. Both objectives prove too ambitious. Germans reach Caucasus foothills and Stalingrad but exhaust themselves. Overextension sets stage for Soviet counterblow.
historical_context: Hitler needed oil. Soviet defenses weakened by Kharkov disaster. Germans initially faced little resistance. But Hitler's decision to pursue both Caucasus AND Stalingrad simultaneously divided his forces. Violated principle of concentration. Set stage for Stalingrad disaster. Last major German offensive success in East.

name: Case Blue: German Summer Offensive - Alternative: Single Objective - Caucasus Only
description: Hitler focuses solely on Caucasus oil. Stalingrad bypassed or masked. Full force Group A to Baku. Potentially captures oil fields. But even if captured, damaged and hard to exploit. Soviet counteroffensive possible elsewhere.
historical_context: Hitler needed oil. Soviet defenses weakened by Kharkov disaster. Germans initially faced little resistance. But Hitler's decision to pursue both Caucasus AND Stalingrad simultaneously divided his forces. Violated principle of concentration. Set stage for Stalingrad disaster. Last major German offensive success in East.

name: Case Blue: German Summer Offensive - Radical: Soviet Defense Holds
description: Case Blue fails to achieve breakthroughs. Soviet defenses (strengthened by not squandering forces at Kharkov in this scenario) hold firm. German summer offensive stalls. Stalingrad never threatened. 1942 becomes stalemate.
historical_context: Hitler needed oil. Soviet defenses weakened by Kharkov disaster. Germans initially faced little resistance. But Hitler's decision to pursue both Caucasus AND Stalingrad simultaneously divided his forces. Violated principle of concentration. Set stage for Stalingrad disaster. Last major German offensive success in East.

name: Battle of Stalingrad Begins - Historical: Urban Warfare Inferno
description: August 23 Luftwaffe raid kills 40,000 civilians, destroys wooden city. German 6th Army enters September 13. Begins house-to-house fighting. Mamayev Kurgan, Red October Factory, Grain Elevator become legendary battlefields. Germans control 90% of city by November but cannot dislodge defenders. Chuikov's 62nd Army clings to Volga bank. Time bought for Uranus.
historical_context: City bore Stalin's name - symbolic importance enormous. Stalin forbade evacuation. Chuikov: 'We will defend the city or die in its ruins.' German tactical superiority neutralized in rubble. Soviet defenders supplied across Volga nightly. Fighting of incredible intensity: life expectancy of Soviet soldier 24 hours, officer 3 days. While Germans focused on city, Soviets prepared counteroffensive.

name: Battle of Stalingrad Begins - Alternative: City Falls
description: Paulus takes city in October. 62nd Army destroyed. Symbolic catastrophe. But German 6th Army still vulnerable to encirclement. Uranus still possible, potentially easier with Germans celebrating in ruins. Strategic outcome similar?
historical_context: City bore Stalin's name - symbolic importance enormous. Stalin forbade evacuation. Chuikov: 'We will defend the city or die in its ruins.' German tactical superiority neutralized in rubble. Soviet defenders supplied across Volga nightly. Fighting of incredible intensity: life expectancy of Soviet soldier 24 hours, officer 3 days. While Germans focused on city, Soviets prepared counteroffensive.

name: Battle of Stalingrad Begins - Radical: Germans Bypass Stalingrad
description: Paulus recognizes city is trap. Masks it with minimal forces. Concentrates on cutting Volga supply routes. Strategic approach vs symbolic obsession. But Hitler would never allow - city's name demands its capture.
historical_context: City bore Stalin's name - symbolic importance enormous. Stalin forbade evacuation. Chuikov: 'We will defend the city or die in its ruins.' German tactical superiority neutralized in rubble. Soviet defenders supplied across Volga nightly. Fighting of incredible intensity: life expectancy of Soviet soldier 24 hours, officer 3 days. While Germans focused on city, Soviets prepared counteroffensive.

name: Operation Uranus: Stalingrad Counteroffensive - Historical: Perfect Encirclement
description: November 19 northern pincer (Southwestern Front) smashes Romanian 3rd Army. November 20 southern pincer (Stalingrad Front) destroys Romanian 4th Army. November 23 pincers meet at Kalach. 6th Army and parts of 4th Panzer Army encircled. 290,000 German and Axis troops trapped. Paulus requests breakout - Hitler orders 'fortress Stalingrad', promises Luftwaffe supply. Manstein's relief attempt (Winter Storm) fails December. 6th Army doomed.
historical_context: Brilliant strategic deception. While Stalin and Chuikov held Stalingrad, Zhukov concentrated forces in secret. Germans knew Romanian flanks were weak but focused on city. Soviet offensive achieved complete surprise. Showed Red Army had learned operational art. Turning point of Eastern Front - from this moment, strategic initiative permanently shifts to USSR.

name: Operation Uranus: Stalingrad Counteroffensive - Alternative: Partial Encirclement/Breakout Success
description: Uranus succeeds but German reaction faster. Paulus orders immediate breakout before Hitler can forbid it. Or encirclement smaller. 6th Army escapes with heavy losses. Still Soviet victory but less complete. Different 1943 balance.
historical_context: Brilliant strategic deception. While Stalin and Chuikov held Stalingrad, Zhukov concentrated forces in secret. Germans knew Romanian flanks were weak but focused on city. Soviet offensive achieved complete surprise. Showed Red Army had learned operational art. Turning point of Eastern Front - from this moment, strategic initiative permanently shifts to USSR.

name: Operation Uranus: Stalingrad Counteroffensive - Radical: Uranus Fails or Detected
description: German intelligence penetrates Soviet preparations. Romanian armies reinforced. Offensive fails or achieves limited success. 6th Army not encircled. Stalingrad siege continues into 1943. Very different war.
historical_context: Brilliant strategic deception. While Stalin and Chuikov held Stalingrad, Zhukov concentrated forces in secret. Germans knew Romanian flanks were weak but focused on city. Soviet offensive achieved complete surprise. Showed Red Army had learned operational art. Turning point of Eastern Front - from this moment, strategic initiative permanently shifts to USSR.

name: Stalingrad Victory and 6th Army Surrender
description: After 76 days encircled, starving, frozen 6th Army surrenders. Paulus capitulates February 2. 91,000 survivors captured (only 6,000 ever return). Total Axis losses at Stalingrad: 850,000. Greatest German defeat. Turning point of war officially recognized.
historical_context: Hitler promoted Paulus to Field Marshal hours before surrender - no German FM had ever surrendered. Paulus ignored hint to commit suicide. 6th Army's agony in encirclement documented by German soldiers' letters. Luftwaffe supply failure complete. Manstein's relief attempt failed December. Soviet ring tightened relentlessly. Final assault January crushed remaining resistance.

name: Battle of Kursk
description: Last major German offensive in East. Operation Citadel attacks Kursk salient July 5. Soviet intelligence (Lucy Ring) revealed plan. Deep defenses prepared. Germans attack into prepared killing zones. Prokhorovka tank battle. German offensive broken after week. Soviet counteroffensives liberate Orel and Belgorod. Strategic initiative permanently to USSR.
historical_context: Hitler delayed Citadel for new Panthers and Tigers. Delay allowed Soviets to prepare eight defensive lines and massive reserves. 6,000 tanks involved. Prokhorovka largest tank battle (though Soviet losses concealed). Germans never again mounted major offensive in East. From Kursk onward, Red Army advances west relentlessly.

name: Battle for Dnieper and Liberation of Kiev
description: After Kursk, relentless Soviet offensives. Dnieper River crossed under fire. Kiev liberated November 6. Ukraine liberation begins. Germans in constant retreat. Soviet operational superiority evident.
historical_context: Hitler ordered Dnieper as defensive line. Soviets crossed at multiple points under fire - massive casualties but successful. Kiev liberated on anniversary of Revolution. Ukraine's liberation would take another year but momentum established.

name: Tehran Conference
description: First meeting of Big Three - Stalin, Roosevelt, Churchill. Overlord confirmed for May 1944. Soviet sphere in Eastern Europe implicitly accepted. Stalin promises to enter Pacific War. Post-war settlement discussed. Stalin dominates conference - strongest position.
historical_context: Stalin's prestige at peak after Stalingrad and Kursk. Refused to leave USSR. Churchill and FDR travel to Tehran. Stalin extracts Overlord commitment and tacit acceptance of Eastern European sphere. Different dynamics than later Yalta - Stalin confident, Western Allies grateful for Soviet victories.

name: Leningrad Siege Lifted
description: After 872 days, longest siege in modern history ends. January offensive drives Germans back. Land corridor to city opened. 1 million died in siege but city never surrendered. Ultimate symbol of Soviet resistance vindicated.
historical_context: Siege began September 8, 1941. 872 days of starvation, bombardment, suffering. Road of Life across Lake Ladoga kept city alive minimally. Cultural life continued impossibly. January 1944 offensive finally drives Germans beyond artillery range. Survivors traumatized but unbroken.

name: Operation Bagration
description: Largest Soviet offensive of war. Named for 1812 Russian general. Launched June 23 (third anniversary of Barbarossa). Four-front coordinated offensive destroys German Army Group Center. 450,000 Germans killed/captured. Minsk liberated. Belarus freed. German losses greater than Stalingrad. Coincides with D-Day, ensures Germans cannot shift forces west.
historical_context: Masterpiece of operational art. Germans expected offensive in Ukraine; Soviets struck Belarus. Complete surprise despite massive preparations. Maskirovka (deception) perfect. Army Group Center destroyed in three weeks - worse than Stalingrad. Timed with D-Day to ensure Germany fought two-front war. Demonstrated Red Army was now world's best.

name: Warsaw Uprising and Soviet Pause
description: Polish Home Army rises against Germans August 1, expecting Soviet support. Red Army halts on Vistula River opposite Warsaw. Stalin forbids assistance. Uprising crushed after 63 days, 200,000 Polish dead. Controversial Soviet inaction - operational necessity or political cynicism eliminating non-communist Polish resistance?
historical_context: Polish government-in-exile ordered uprising assuming Soviet help. Red Army had advanced 450 miles in six weeks - operational pause arguably necessary. But Stalin's refusal to allow Allied airdrops or provide support clearly political. Wanted communist Poland, not London Poles. Uprising's suppression eliminated non-communist resistance, easing Soviet control. One of war's most controversial episodes.

name: Jassy-Kishinev and Romania's Switch
description: Massive offensive destroys German-Romanian forces. Romania switches sides August 23 - King Michael arrests Antonescu, joins Allies. Bulgarian armistice September. Hungary invaded October. Axis satellites collapsing like dominoes. Balkans falling to Red Army.
historical_context: Romania's oil vital to Germany. Soviet offensive encircles and destroys German 6th Army (rebuilt after Stalingrad) and Romanian forces. King Michael's coup switches Romania to Allied side. Ploesti oil lost. Bulgaria follows suit. Red Army pours into Balkans. Demonstrates Soviet ability to coordinate political warfare with military operations.

name: Red Army Enters Yugoslavia and Balkans
description: Combined Soviet-Yugoslav Partisan offensive liberates Belgrade October 20. Red Army coordinates with Tito's forces. Communist Yugoslavia's independence from USSR seeded here - Tito's forces liberated own country with Soviet help, not Soviet occupation. Bulgaria, Romania, parts of Hungary occupied.
historical_context: Unlike other Eastern European countries, Yugoslavia largely liberated itself under Tito. Soviet forces assisted but Tito's communist credentials and military success gave him independence Stalin couldn't challenge. Belgrade liberation joint operation. Different from Poland, Romania, etc. where Red Army arrived as liberator-occupiers.

name: Vistula-Oder Offensive
description: Largest offensive in history. Four fronts, 2.2 million men, 7,000 tanks advance 300 miles in 20 days. Warsaw liberated January 17 (ruins). Krakow liberated. Oder River reached 60km from Berlin by February 2. Speed shocks even Soviets. Germans collapsing.
historical_context: Originally planned for January 20 but advanced to January 12 to relieve Western Allies' Bulge pressure (controversially - Stalin claimed this, Western historians debate). Fastest major offensive of war. German resistance shattered. Shows Red Army operational superiority absolute. Zhukov reaches Berlin approaches while Western Allies still in Germany's west.

name: Yalta Conference
description: Big Three meet with Red Army 60km from Berlin. Stalin in strongest position. Poland's fate sealed - communist government, borders shifted west. German occupation zones agreed. United Nations charter. Soviet Pacific War entry confirmed. Controversial concessions to Stalin reflect military reality.
historical_context: Met in Crimea February 4-11. FDR dying, Churchill weakened. Stalin dominant - Red Army controls Eastern Europe. Poland's borders shifted west (gains German territory, loses eastern Poland to USSR). Free elections promised but meaningless. Soviet sphere recognized implicitly. Criticised as Western betrayal but reflected power realities.

name: Battle of Berlin
description: Final assault begins April 16. Zhukov from east (Seelow Heights), Konev from south. 2.5 million Soviet troops, 6,000 tanks, 40,000 artillery pieces. Brutal urban combat. Reichstag stormed April 30 (day Hitler suicides). Red flag raised over Reichstag May 2. Berlin garrison surrenders May 2. Symbolic victory - Red Army takes Hitler's capital.
historical_context: Stalin insists Soviets take Berlin despite casualties. Zhukov-Konev rivalry exploited to motivate commanders. Seelow Heights bloodbath. Urban combat through Berlin ruins. Hitler suicides April 30. May 2 city surrenders. Cost: 80,000 Soviet dead, 280,000 wounded. But ultimate symbolic achievement - Red Army conquered Nazi capital.

name: Victory in Europe
description: Germany surrenders unconditionally May 8 (West), May 9 (Soviet time). Great Patriotic War ends. 27 million Soviet dead. But Nazi Germany destroyed. Red Army controls Eastern Europe from Stettin to Trieste. Superpower emerged from ruins.
historical_context: Capitulation signed May 8 at 11:01pm (May 9 Soviet time). Stalin insisted on separate ceremony in Berlin May 9. Victory Day celebrated May 9 in USSR vs May 8 in West - symbolic of division emerging. Price incomprehensible: 27 million dead (17M civilian, 10M military). But USSR emerged as superpower controlling half Europe.

name: Manchurian Strategic Offensive
description: Three months after German surrender, USSR enters Pacific War as promised. August 9 massive offensive destroys Japanese Kwantung Army in Manchuria. Three-pronged assault from Mongolia, Siberia, Vladivostok. Japanese defenses shattered in days. Manchuria, Sakhalin, Kuriles occupied. Korea to 38th parallel. Demonstrates Red Army still world's best despite Germany focus.
historical_context: Promised at Yalta to enter Pacific War three months after German surrender. Stalin kept promise exactly - three months to the day. 1.5 million Soviet troops attack 700,000 Japanese. Kwantung Army (once elite, now depleted) destroyed in 11 days. Operation shows Soviet operational mastery transferable across theaters. Secured territorial concessions (Kuriles, Sakhalin, Port Arthur). Divided Korea at 38th parallel. Cold War in Asia begins.

name: Potsdam Conference and Cold War Dawn
description: Final wartime conference. Stalin only original leader - Truman replaced FDR (died April), Attlee replaced Churchill mid-conference (election). Soviet domination of Eastern Europe reality. German administration discussed. Atomic bomb revealed to Stalin. Japanese surrender terms. Cold War emerging from wartime alliance's corpse.
historical_context: July 17-August 2. Met in occupied Berlin - Soviet power evident. Stalin confident, Truman new and uncertain. Atomic bomb tested during conference - Truman tells Stalin who pretends ignorance (knew from spies). Polish borders confirmed. German reparations disputed. Eastern European governments communist despite free election promises. Alliance fracturing. Churchill's Iron Curtain speech (1946) would articulate what Potsdam made evident.
